[They] replied, "We shall be able to rescue and protect them."
"Seventh: From this time forth, for as long as the future endures, will you all be able to constantly provide offerings to the Triple Gem according to your capacity?
(They reply: We can provide offerings."
"Eighth, from this time forth until the end of the future, will you all be able to remain constantly filial toward your parents and respectful in serving your teachers and elders?
(They replied: "We shall be able to show filial piety and respect."
"Ninth, from this time forward until the end of the future, will you all be able to constantly abandon all laziness and diligently seek the Buddha-way?
(They replied: "We shall diligently seek it."

"Number ten: From this time forward, for as long as the future endures, when various afflictions arise regarding the five sensory objects, will you be able to subdue the mind? (Answer: We shall be able to subdue it."
Eleventh: From this time forth, throughout the remainder of your lives until the end of the future, you vow to deliver infinite sentient beings.
Are you able to deliver them? (They answer: We are able to deliver them.
Twelfth: From this time forth, until the end of the future and throughout all successive lives, you vow to sever afflictions that are inexhaustible.
Are you able to sever them? (He replies: "I am able to sever them."
Thirteenth: From this time forth, for as long as the future endures, you vow to study immeasurable Dharma gates.
Are you able to study them? (He replies: I am able to study them.
Fourteenth: From this time forth, until the end of the future, you shall vow to achieve the unsurpassed path of the Buddha.
Are you able to achieve it? (They answer: We are able to achieve it.
Tenth, the ritual for manifesting the essence of the precepts: The Bodhisattva Precept Master strikes the sounding block and says:

"O sons of the Buddha, since you have been able to give rise to these fourteen kinds of profound and vast vows, I shall now rise from my seat to prostrate and address the Buddhas currently dwelling in the ten directions and all the Bodhisattvas, so as to inspire you."
Regarding the precept-substance of the Perfect Teaching (Yuanzong), you should listen with single-minded attention and contemplate it with careful reflection.

You should know that when I have finished my first formal announcement (*jñapti*), the wondrous and virtuous dharma of the precepts throughout the worlds of the ten directions will all tremble by the power of the mental karma.
When I have finished my second formal announcement, the wondrous and virtuous dharma of the precepts throughout the worlds of the ten directions will cover you like clouds or a canopy.

At the crown of your head. When I have finished my threefold proclamation, the wondrous and virtuous precepts of the ten directions shall flow from the aperture at your crown into your body and mind, filling your primary retribution and remaining as the seed of Buddhahood throughout the limits of the future.
This is the unconditioned (anabhisaṃskāra) precept-body, an outflow-free (anāsrava) form-dharma, attained through the influence of your superior wholesome mind. Therefore, you—
One should receive this with utmost sincerity and reverence. Next, regarding the ritual for the formal conferral of the precept-body (*śīla-ātmabhāva*), the *Sūtra* states:

"The Bodhisattva who receives [the precepts] shall not rise from his seat, but remain as before in a long-kneeling posture (*pragṛhīta-jānu*). The Bodhisattva who confers [the precepts] shall rise..."

Seated before the Buddha image, one should reverently make offerings and prostrate at the feet of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas currently dwelling throughout the ten directions, and offer this formal declaration (the text of the declaration follows below).

Now, according to the established ritual, the two Ācāryas descend from their seats first, followed by the Bodhisattva Preceptor. Upon reaching the front of the Buddha image, the two masters divide [their positions].

The attendants stand to the left and right; the Preceptor stands in the center and offers incense. Entering into contemplation, they perform three prostrations. Kneeling long with palms joined, they address the assembly, saying:
"I look up to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the boundless and limitless worlds of the ten directions. Now, at [Name of Province] [Name of Temple]..."
In this regard, there is a bodhisattva named [Name] who, before me, the bodhisattva named [Name], has formally received the bodhisattva precepts up to three times.

May I serve as his witness. I pray that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the boundless and limitless worlds of the ten directions—the foremost true sages, whether manifest or unmanifest—at all times and in all places, for all sentient beings...
The present Awakened One also acts as a witness for the bodhisattva [Name] who has received the precepts; out of compassion, out of compassion, out of great compassion.
This follows the scriptural text. Thus, there are three recitations of the "white" (śukla), which constitute the three rounds of the *karmavācanā*.

Once the *karmavācanā* has been completed according to the Dharma, the recipient immediately obtains the precepts. The Precept Master and the two other masters perform a prostration and then return to their original seats.
This is not like the method for receiving full ordination (*upasampadā*) within the Sangha, where ten masters sit together; here, it is sufficient that the *karmavācanā* be performed.
Eleventh, the Method for Proclaiming the Characteristics of the Precepts.

First, according to the text of the *Bodhisattva-karman-sūtra*, after three rounds of formal announcement to the Noble Ones, one immediately attains the sublime and virtuous essence of the Bodhisattva’s Threefold Aggregate of Precepts (*tri-śikṣā-saṃvara*).
This follows the *Brahmajāla-sūtra*, which next proclaims the ten grave precepts and forty [minor] precepts of the Bodhisattva.
Regarding the eight minor precepts, one should cause them to be known and maintained so as to protect the body. The Bodhisattva Precept Master strikes the sounding block and says:

"O Sons of the Buddha, there are ten inexhaustible bodhisattva precepts that should be received and upheld. Each shall recite its dharma-name. (Having recited them, he says: "The Ten Inexhaustible...")

Regarding "exhaustive precepts" (*kṣaya-śīla*): the *Adornment Sūtra* (*Ābharaṇa-sūtra*) states, "The precepts of all bodhisattvas, whether ordinary or sagely, take the mind as their essence. Therefore, when the mind is exhausted, the precepts are also exhausted; yet because the mind is inexhaustible, the precepts are also inexhaustible. Hence they are called 'inexhaustible precepts.'"

"O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the interval until the end of the future, you must under no circumstances intentionally kill living beings.
If you should violate this, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva, and you will lose the dharmas of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones.
Can you maintain the precept of non-killing? [The answer is: "I can maintain it."

"O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entire interval until the end of the future, you must not intentionally commit theft for a second time.
If you should violate this, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva; you shall lose the Dharma of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones.
Can you maintain the precept against stealing? [He] replies: "I can maintain it."

"O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the interval extending to the end of the future, you must not intentionally engage in sexual desire for a third time.
If you should violate this, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva; you will lose the Dharma of the forty-two levels of sages and saints.
Can you maintain the precept against sexual misconduct? [The respondent] replies: "I can maintain it."

"O Son of the Buddha, from this body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the interval until the end of the future, you must not intentionally utter false speech as the fourth [precept].
If you should violate it, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva, and you will lose the dharmas of the forty-two worthies and sages.
Can you maintain the precept of non-false speech? [The answer is: "I can maintain it."

"O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of Buddhahood, throughout the interval extending to the end of the future, you must not intentionally sell alcohol as the fifth precept.
If you should violate it, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva; you will lose the dharmas of the forty-two worthy sages.
Can you maintain this precept against selling alcohol? [The respondent] replied: "I can maintain it."

From this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entire span of the future, the sixth [precept] prohibits one from intentionally speaking of the faults and transgressions of lay or ordained Bodhisattvas, whether they be *bhikṣus* or *bhikṣuṇīs*.

Should one violate this, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; one loses the forty-two dharmas of the noble ones (*ārya*) and is unable to speak of the four kinds of precepts against transgression.
Will you uphold it? (He answers: I can uphold it.
Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of Buddhahood, throughout the entire extent of the future, during that interval, the seventh [precept] must not be violated:
one must not praise oneself and disparage others. If one violates this, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva, and one loses the forty-two [bodhisattva precepts].
"Regarding the dharmas of the noble ones: can you maintain the precept of not praising yourself and disparaging others? [He] answers, "I can maintain it.
"O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of Buddhahood, throughout the entire extent of the future," [he says].

Eighth: One must not, out of stinginess, harbor malice or inflict injury. If one commits such an offense, it is not the conduct of a bodhisattva; one loses the forty-two dharmas of the worthy and holy ones.
Can you uphold the precept against stinginess, malice, and inflicting injury? (He answers: I can uphold it.
